# #162 — lane_upsert fails to create new lane when status omitted (NOT NULL violation; breaks bilby/skippy writes)

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: bug
Created: 2026-06-19T14:22:23Z
Updated: 2026-06-19T15:02:21Z
Closed: 2026-06-19T14:52:36Z

---

## Bug

`lane_upsert` fails to CREATE a new session lane when the caller omits `status`, with:
```
null value in column "status" of relation "ob_session_lanes" violates not-null constraint
```

## Impact (live)

- **240 failures in 24h** on hosted OB (`skippy-oc` / 10.71.1.21): **69 bilby, 171 skippy**, 2026-06-18→19.
- This is an **upstream cause** of Hermes lane writes not landing — when the first write to a new `session_key` fails server-side, the Hermes side spools it and (per rtech-hermes#84's F2) mistakes "spooled" for "saved." So the rtech-hermes spooled-vs-saved symptom has a real open-brain root cause.
- It is NOT the previously-suspected "wedged worker, fix with a bounce" issue — both workers were healthy; this is a deterministic DB constraint violation. A bounce never fixed it; it only changed which session_keys were new.

## Root cause

`src/tools/lane-upsert.ts:126` set `status = args.status ?? null` and bound that NULL into the INSERT VALUES for the `NOT NULL` `status` column (default `'active'`). An explicit NULL overrides the column default → constraint violation on INSERT. The ON CONFLICT/UPDATE path guards on `$3 IS NULL` and preserves the stored status, so existing-lane updates succeeded (masking the bug; only new lanes fail).

## Fix

PR fixes it with a separate insert value (`insertStatus = args.status ?? 'active'` as `$24`) for the INSERT VALUES, keeping `$3` nullable for the ON CONFLICT preserve-logic, and re-points the `ended_at` CASE from `EXCLUDED.status` to `$3` (required — otherwise a status-omitted update would reactivate a wrapped/archived lane). Regression test added. Full suite 726 pass, typecheck clean.

## Follow-up
- The mock test harness can't fire the real constraint; a live-DB integration test would be a stronger guard (noted as optional).
- Deploy to hosted OB (`com.rico.open-brain` on 10.71.1.21) needed to actually stop the live failures.

## Discussion (3)

### rodaddy — 2026-06-19T14:42:34Z

## ⚠️ Deployed fix REGRESSED lane_upsert — still 100% failing, new error (2026-06-19)

Verified live from Bilby's real Hermes interpreter, replaying an actual stuck `lane_upsert` spool entry against hosted OB (commit `b49e5d4` deployed). The original NOT-NULL error is gone, but it's been **replaced by a new failure**:

```
lane_upsert body=Database error during lane upsert: could not determine data type of parameter $3
```

**This still breaks every lane_upsert.** The "240/24h stopped after restart" reading was a **false positive** — the service had only ~40s uptime with no lane traffic, so no new errors had a chance to fire. The first real lane write (mine, just now) fails.

### Root cause of the regression

The fix repointed the INSERT VALUES status slot to `$24` (`insertStatus`), leaving `$3` (`status`, `null` when omitted) used **only** in `CASE WHEN` comparisons:

- `status = CASE WHEN $3 IS NULL THEN ... ELSE EXCLUDED.status END` (line ~189)
- `ended_at = CASE WHEN $3 = 'wrapped' OR $3 = 'archived' ... WHEN $3 = 'active' ...` (lines ~204-208)

Postgres infers a bind parameter's type from a typed usage site (e.g. a column position). With `$3` no longer bound into the `status` column and used only in `IS NULL` / equality-vs-string-literal, **its type is undeterminable at plan time** → `could not determine data type of parameter $3`. A real DB-backed query exercises this; a mock harness does not (the PR honestly flagged the mock limitation).

### Fix — cast `$3` to its column type everywhere it's used

`status` is `TEXT`, so pin the type with an explicit cast (behavior identical; null stays null, comparisons unchanged):

```sql
status = CASE WHEN $3::text IS NULL THEN ob_session_lanes.status ELSE EXCLUDED.status END,
...
ended_at = CASE WHEN $3::text = 'wrapped' OR $3::text = 'archived'
           THEN COALESCE(ob_session_lanes.ended_at, NOW())
           WHEN $3::text = 'active' THEN NULL
           ELSE ob_session_lanes.ended_at END
```

**Also verify:** `$24` (`insertStatus`) is actually appended to the params array (the array tail wasn't fully visible) — if `insertStatus` isn't bound at position 24, that's a second bug.

**Strongly recommend** a DB-backed regression test (real pool, not mock) covering: (a) new lane, status omitted → row created with `status='active'`; (b) omitted-status update of a `wrapped` lane → `status` stays `wrapped`, `ended_at` unchanged. The mock test can't catch type-inference or constraint failures — this regression is the proof.
